input: Scheduled ventures run: continue work on the repo aiming to develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue generating software products (standing brief in prompts/ventures/prompt-1.md)
task: New venture pdf-plan-takeoff: browser PDF takeoff (length/area/count, snapping) with each view's scale note read and checked against the sheet's dimension strings; half-size print detection
errors: First room-area eval read 2 of 298 within 2%: these sets' plans are raster tiles, so the vector-only flood saw no walls; added image decoding, still 5 of 298, reported as is
A dimension-check pass first matched the opaque text-mask rectangles Revit draws behind dimension text (fill edges); fixed by matching strokes only

doc_friction.issue: Start-here row was open-tennis-robots again (CAD bolt tails); the row's own 'Left recently' note says 8 sessions in 2 days left it for the same reason, yet the buildable item still leads the row

The deep construction flagships (xer-schedule-check, league-schedule-generator) list almost only items needing real outside inputs in next:, so a run must read ~2000-character rows to find nothing buildable; NEXT.md lists more of the same

deviations.why: Took no flagship row: the start-here row (open-tennis-robots bolt tails) has no market path and the other reachable flagships' next items need real outside inputs. Started a new construction venture instead (brief: 'also focus on starting new ones'; goals.md construction direction), with a paid incumbent (Bluebeam/PlanSwift) and a feature none of them has (dimension-checked scale, half-size print detection).
deviations.did: Built pdf-plan-takeoff with page, CLI, tests, evaluation on 14 public drawing sets
deviations.result: Scale check confirmed on 44 pages, half-size flagged on 43 of 44 simulated prints, 0 false alarms on 180 originals; fill-area tool weak (5 of 298 rooms within 2%) and labelled experimental

goal: Ship a new construction venture with real business potential and an honest measured differentiator
notes: Local checks: python3 platform/ci/run_venture_tests.py pdf-plan-takeoff drawing-set-index submittal-register bank-statement-pdf-to-csv pdf-accessibility-tag-check dupehound -> 6 suites run, 0 failed (after fixing the FAQ JSON-LD to match visible questions, platform/pages/faq-visible.test.mjs). check_posts.py ok. Page driven in Playwright on the sample (confirmed and half-size verdicts, 120.5 SF office fill, length on corners) and on two real rotated sheets (fb-20180925 p2 inferred 1/8 from 19/29 dims; of-20190525 p2 confirmed 35/49), no page errors. Evals in ventures/pdf-plan-takeoff/eval/. pdf-parser-sync test now lists five copies; dupehound guard updated.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a senior engineer building a PDF vector reader, scale/dimension checker with a 14-set evaluation, a canvas takeoff page and tests from scratch

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
